instrument_name: SDCL Title 60 Labor and Employment, full official text (ch. 60-11 wages, hours and conditions)
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: Min wage statutory base USD 8.50/h indexed each Jan 1 by CPI-U (US city avg, all items) Aug-over-Aug, increase rounded UP to nearest 5 cents, never decreased; DLR publishes by Oct 15 (60-11-3.2). Excluded: opportunity-wage employees, babysitters, outside salespersons, seasonal amusement/recreation establishments, organized camps, religious/nonprofit educational conference centres (7-month or 33.3% receipts test). Tipped (>USD 35/month tips): cash wage >= 50% of min wage with make-up each pay period (60-11-3.1). Under-20 opportunity wage per FLSA s.6 (60-11-4.1). Apprentices/learners/persons with developmental disability exempt only with DLR permit (60-11-5). Pay at least once each calendar month or on regular agreed paydays designated in advance; by check, cash or direct deposit unless employer and employee agree another form (60-11-9). Final pay on discharge and on resignation: not later than the next regular payday for those hours, or as soon after as employee returns employer property (60-11-10, 60-11-11). 60-11-8..23 apply to cash wages only (60-11-14). No state overtime, pay-statement, deduction-authorisation, paid sick leave or vacation-payout section in Title 60 (full-text keyword scan).

instrument_name: SDCL Title 61 Reemployment Assistance (unemployment compensation), full official text
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base USD 15,000 on and after 2015-01-01 (fixed in statute, not indexed); 'employment' for the base includes service under another state's UI law, so wages already reported to another state count toward the SD 15,000 (61-1-46). New employer: 1.2% year 1, 1.0% thereafter while positive balance until experience-rated; construction (NAICS 23) 6% / 3% (61-5-24). Experience-rated: schedule A/B/C chosen by average high cost multiplier ratio (<1.30 A; 1.30-1.50 B; >=1.50 C) (61-5-25); 2026+ table (SL 2025 ch 199): Schedule A 0.00%-9.39%, B 0.00%-9.24%, C 0.00%-8.52% (61-5-25.7). Administrative fee 0.08% from calendar year 2026 for every experience-rated employer (was 0.02% if reserve ratio <2.25%) (61-5-28.1). Investment fee 0.55% non-rated; rated 0.00%-0.53% by reserve ratio, hold-harmless at 1987 rate (61-5-29). Fund-balance surcharge 0.1%-1.5% if fund < USD 11 m at quarter-end (61-5-28). Fees may not be deducted from employee wages. Domestic service covered at USD 1,000 cash in a quarter (61-1-19); agricultural at USD 20,000 in a quarter or 10 workers in 20 weeks (61-1-17).

instrument_name: SD DLR Minimum Wage page (2026 and 2027 rates)
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-tipped USD 11.85/h eff. 2026-01-01; USD 12.30/h eff. 2027-01-01. Tipped cash wage USD 5.925/h eff. 2026-01-01; USD 6.15/h eff. 2027-01-01. Employer keeps a record of all tips. Exemptions as SDCL 60-11-3/3.1/4.1/5.

instrument_name: SD DLR State Minimum Wage posters 2026 and 2027 (English)
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 poster USD 11.85/h, tipped cash wage USD 5.925; 2027 poster USD 12.30/h, tipped USD 6.15. Poster states no state statute requires the posting (courtesy). Spanish versions exist (min-wage-poster-{year}-spanish.pdf, not downloaded).

instrument_name: SDCL ch. 21-18 Garnishment of debts and property, full text
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary garnishment cap per workweek = lesser of (1) 20% of disposable earnings or (2) disposable earnings minus 40 x federal minimum hourly wage (or state minimum wage if greater) LESS USD 25/week for each dependent family member residing with the debtor (more protective than CCPA 25%/30x). Support orders: 50% (supporting another spouse/child) / 60% otherwise, 55% / 65% for arrears older than 12 weeks (21-18-52). Garnishee withholds nonexempt earnings through the last payroll period ending on or before 120 days from the summons. Exemptions only per 21-18-51/52 (21-18-53).

instrument_name: SDCL ch. 25-7A Collection of child support, full text (income withholding; state directory of new hires)
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: New hire: every employer reports each newly hired employee (incl. rehired/reinstated; anyone required to give a W-4): name, address, SSN of employee; employer name, address, FEIN; within 20 days of hire or, if electronic, two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; on W-4 or equivalent; multistate electronic reporters may designate one state and notify HHS in writing (25-7A-3.3). IWO: amount withheld for support and arrearage may not exceed 50% of wages etc. (25-7A-32); first deduction from the first payment after service; remit to the Department within 7 business days after payday; payor may deduct up to USD 3/month expense fee (25-7A-34); multiple orders: priority to current support within the 25-7A-32 cap (25-7A-35).

instrument_name: SDCL 12-3-5 (time off to vote) and 16-13-41.1 (jury service protection)
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: Voting: employee entitled to 2 consecutive hours off while polls are open (unless 2 consecutive off-duty hours exist) with NO deduction from usual salary or wages; employer may set the hours (12-3-5). Jury: no discharge or suspension for jury service (16-13-41.1); pay for jury time is at employer discretion (DLR Q&A, US-SDS5-011).

instrument_name: SDCL ch. 33A-2 Military personnel (National Guard active-duty protections)
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: A SD resident National Guard member ordered to active duty by a Governor or the President has all protections of persons on federal active duty under the SCRA (chapter read by keyword scan only; no state paid military-leave duty for private employers located). Federal USERRA governs reemployment.

instrument_name: SD DLR Termination of Employment page
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: At-will employment; final wages on quit or discharge due not later than the next regular stated payday for those hours, or as soon after as the employee returns employer property. Off-duty tobacco use protected; jury service protected.

instrument_name: SD DLR 'South Dakota Labor and Employment Laws - What You Need to Know' (Q&A), Rev. 01/2026
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: No state law requiring rest/meal breaks, holiday pay, paid vacation or sick leave, or severance. Final pay on quit/discharge: next regular payday; employer may hold until property returned. Withholding vacation pay for failure to give notice is a matter of employer-employee agreement (no statutory payout rule). Jury time paid or unpaid at employer discretion. Q&A quotes the 2026 minimum wage USD 11.85.

instrument_name: SD DLR Compensatory Time/Overtime and Holiday Pay pages
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: 'South Dakota has no labor laws concerning compensatory (comp) time or overtime' - FLSA only. Holiday pay page (https://dlr.sd.gov/employment_laws/holiday_pay.aspx): 'South Dakota has no law requiring holiday pay.' The overtime page still describes the 2024 DOL salary-threshold rule (federal status: see FED unit).

instrument_name: SD DLR Reemployment Assistance Tax - Wage Reporting page
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly wage report filed online (Internet Quarterly Wage Reporting System; optional comma-delimited upload in a DLR format) or CD/DVD ASCII file; due (received by) Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31; zero-wage reports required. Domestic employers with prior approval file annually (Form 21D & 21E). Corrections on Form 21C. Late filing USD 25 per month or fraction; late payment USD 25 per month or fraction; interest 1.5% per month. Page states min 0% / max 9.5% (pre-2026 statement; SDCL 61-5-25.7 governs). Wages include vacation, sick pay, gifts/awards, employee 401(k)-type deferrals, cafeteria/Sec. 125 amounts, profit sharing; exclude non-required severance/dismissal pay, employer 401(k)/403(b)/408(k)/408(p)/457 contributions, elected officials, work-study students. Tips reported if > USD 20/month. Family exemptions by entity type (sole prop: owner's children under 21, spouse, parents; corporations none).

instrument_name: SD DLR RA Tax Unit 'Instructions for Reporting Wages by CD or DVD' (E/S record format)
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: 85-byte fixed records. E (employer) record: type 'E'; pay-qtr (last month of quarter, 2 digits); pay-yr (2 digits); 6-digit DLR account no.; 9-digit FEIN; employer name 35; state code 46 at 74-75. S (employee) records follow: SSN 9 (2-10); last name 20; first name 10; middle initial 1; total quarterly wages 9 (56-64, implied 2 decimals, leading zeros, positive only); taxable wages 9 (65-73); state code 46; DLR account 6 (76-81). Undated 2-page PDF; the online comma-delimited upload format was not obtained.

instrument_name: SD DLR New Hire Reporting Center page
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers report newly hired and rehired employees (full-time, part-time, student, temporary) to the New Hire Reporting Center (DLR, PO Box 4700 Aberdeen; fax 888-835-8659). Report name and SSN exactly as on the Social Security card. Quarterly UI reports do not satisfy new-hire reporting.

instrument_name: SD DLR Youth Employment page (SDCL ch. 60-12)
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: Under 16: no hazardous occupation; max 4 h per school day / 20 h per school week; 8 h per non-school day / 40 h per non-school week; not after 10 p.m. on a school night. Under 14: not during school hours, not after 7 p.m. The stricter of state/federal (29 CFR 570) applies. Exceptions: child actors, gas pumping, detasselling, parental employment, support necessity (permit), agricultural equipment.

instrument_name: SDCL ch. 22-40 Identity crimes, ss. 22-40-19 to 22-40-26 (breach of system security notice)
authority: South Dakota Legislature (Legislative Research Council)
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information = name + SSN, driver licence/government ID no., financial account no. with access code, health information, or employer-assigned ID + access code/biometric. Information holder notifies affected SD residents within 60 days of discovery; notifies the Attorney General when > 250 residents; consumer reporting agencies notified (22-40-24). No SD statute located requiring SSN truncation on pay statements (keyword scan of Titles 60, 61 and ch. 22-40).

instrument_name: SD DLR Reemployment Assistance Tax FAQ (registration, liability, out-of-state reporting, rates)
authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: 1+ worker in 20 weeks, or USD 1,500 wages in a quarter; FUTA + another state's UI; acquisition; agricultural USD 20,000/quarter or 10 workers in 20 weeks; domestic USD 1,000/quarter; 501(c)(3) with 4+ workers in 20 weeks. Out-of-state employers: SD residents working in SD and out-of-state employees working in SD more than 90 days are reported to SD; fewer than 90 days to the home state; non-localized workers to the state of direction and control; 'Do not report based on residency'. New employer: 1.20% (construction 6.00%) year 1, 1.00% (3.00%) years 2-3, + investment fee 0.55%, admin fee n/a. Administrative fee 0.08% for 2026 and after for experience-rated employers. Domestic employers may elect annual reporting (Form DE by Dec 31). Registration online gives account number and rate immediately.
